svg.title: Exit-First Bridge and Credit Line Architecture
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-06-bridge-and-credit-line-architecture; chapter number: 11; chart type: org_architecture; title: Exit-First Bridge and Credit Line Architecture; subtitle: Short-term, equity-sized debt underwritten on the sale or refinance; caption: Every bridge loan has an exit, and the lender asks about it before almost anything else; each capital route around it is priced and capped differently.; assumptions note: Leverage caps conflict across practitioners, from 70% to 80% combined LTV. Line of credit costs assume interest only on a $20K draw from a $50K line over 6 months.; note: Attributed to Michael Daniel Investments, SEI Mortgage (Ryan Marks), Easy Lending USA, Rene Nelson, Fast Business Lending and The Mortgage Man (Steve Ferguson).; center: role: Bridge lender underwriting the exit; headcount: Single lender seat per loan; focus: Primary exit plus a second exit matched to slow or hot market conditions; spokes: role: Buy-before-you-sell homeowner; type: Residential bridge; kpi: 70% to 80% combined LTV over 6 to 12 months; SEI caps at 75%; role: Investor LLC borrower; type: Investor bridge; kpi: 75% at 2+ deals and FICO 620+, 72.5% at 1 deal, 70% new; 12 to 18 months; role: Private bridge capital; type: Private lender; kpi: 11% to 12%, not index-tied; interest-only about 1% of balance per month; role: Business line of credit; type: Revolving credit; kpi: About $583 at a bank vs $1,800 to $3,488 online on a $20K draw
